questions.question: What does a vehicle inspection report do?

options.text: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
Make sure the vehicle is inspected regularly
Hold people responsible for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell the motor carrier about problems that need fixing
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the carrier about any problems that need to be fixed.

questions.question: Alcohol can be removed from your body by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Waiting
questions.explanation: Your liver removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The only way to sober up is to give your body time to remove the alcohol naturally.

questions.question: When exiting a vehicle, you must maintain ____ with your vehicle at all times.
questions.correctAnswerText: Three points of contact
questions.explanation: When exiting your vehicle, face the vehicle and keep three points of contact at all times. If you are exiting a bus, hold the handrail. Exiting incorrectly can cause you to fail the test.

questions.question: During a pre-trip inspection, look for all of the following, except:

options.text: Tires with too much air pressure

questions.correctAnswerText: Tires made by different manufacturers
questions.explanation: Check your tires for proper tread depth, cracks, correct air pressure, and even wear. Front tires need at least 4/32 inch tread depth. Other tires need at least 2/32 inch. All tires should be the same size.

questions.question: If you feel drowsy while driving, you should:

options.text: Keep driving and finish your trip
Drive faster to reach your destination sooner
Safely pull off the road and take a nap

questions.correctAnswerText: Safely pull off the road and take a nap
questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, stop and get some sleep. Driving while tired is a major cause of deadly accidents.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Cannot be used on vehicles carrying hazardous materials
Help drivers see a wider area

questions.correctAnswerText: Help drivers see a wider area
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved mirrors on many large vehicles. They let drivers see a wider area than flat mirrors. However, objects appear smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Refueling a bus while passengers are on board is:

options.text: Recommended, but only if passengers are told about it
Recommended, but only if time is limited

questions.correctAnswerText: Not recommended
questions.explanation: Do not refuel a bus while passengers are on board unless absolutely necessary. Never refuel a bus with passengers inside an enclosed building.

questions.question: The more alcohol in your body:

options.text: The faster your liver will break it down
The less effect it will have on you
The longer it will take to leave your body

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer it will take to leave your body
questions.explanation: Your body removes alcohol at a fixed rate. The more alcohol you drink, the longer it takes your body to remove it.

questions.question: You can avoid distracted driving by:
questions.correctAnswerText: Pre-setting your radio stations
questions.explanation: Avoid distracted driving by pre-setting radio stations, planning your route ahead of time, avoiding difficult conversations while driving, adjusting mirrors before you leave, and not eating, drinking, or smoking while driving.

questions.question: What should you do if the braking system cannot build hydraulic pressure?

options.text: Push the brake pedal down as far as it will go

questions.correctAnswerText: Shift to a lower gear
questions.explanation: If your hydraulic brakes will not build pressure, try shifting to a lower gear, pumping the brakes, and/or using the emergency brake.

questions.question: If your brakes fail going downhill, why should you decide what to do quickly?

options.text: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
The longer you wait, the more vehicles will get out of your way.
The longer you wait, the slower your vehicle will go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go.
questions.explanation: When your brakes fail going downhill, you must act quickly. The longer you wait, the faster your vehicle will go and the harder it will be to stop.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a reason to use your mirrors?

options.text: You are looking at fuel prices.

questions.correctAnswerText: You are looking at fuel prices.
questions.explanation: Check your mirrors regularly while driving. This is especially important when turning, changing lanes, merging, and making tight maneuvers.

questions.question: When you approach your vehicle before a trip, what should you look for as a sign of trouble?

options.text: A puddle of oil under the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: A puddle of oil under the vehicle
questions.explanation: Before your trip, look under the vehicle for fresh leaks of oil, coolant, grease, or fuel. A fresh puddle of any of these fluids means there is a safety problem with your vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true?

options.text: It is safe to drive on a tire with one or two missing lug nuts.
A cracked lock ring on a rim is safe if you drive slower than 55 mph.
A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.

questions.correctAnswerText: A missing clamp on a rim is dangerous and must be fixed.
questions.explanation: Missing clamps, spacers, studs, or lugs are dangerous. Mismatched, bent, or cracked lock rings are also dangerous. Check that your tires and rims are in good condition before driving.

questions.question: If a vehicle has an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), what should happen when the vehicle starts?

options.text: The ABS indicator light should turn on, then quickly turn off.
The steering wheel will not move until the air tanks are full.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS indicator light should turn on, then quickly turn off.
questions.explanation: When you start a vehicle with an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS), the indicator light should come on and then turn off. If the light stays on, the ABS is not working correctly.

questions.question: When stopped, what should a bus driver do?

options.text: Warn passengers about hazards as they exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn passengers about hazards as they exit.
questions.explanation: When stopped, a bus driver should warn passengers to watch their step when leaving the bus.

questions.question: When should you adjust your mirrors?

options.text: When stopped at a traffic signal

questions.correctAnswerText: Before starting your trip
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start each trip. Any attached trailer should be straight when you adjust the mirrors.

questions.question: What is a Class 1 hazardous material?
questions.correctAnswerText: An explosive
questions.explanation: Explosives are in hazardous materials Class 1.

questions.question: What should you do when traveling long distances?
questions.correctAnswerText: Take rest breaks.
questions.explanation: To avoid fatigue on a long trip, take a break after every 100 miles or two hours of driving. Driving through the night increases the risk of fatigue.

questions.question: Who is responsible for safe vehicle operation?
questions.correctAnswerText: The driver
questions.explanation: The driver is responsible for safe vehicle operation. Always perform a vehicle inspection before driving.
